claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 17. He's not in college or anything like that at the moment – he finished school but isn't studying anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. 

Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to ask: Is Alex working? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just at home with me right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. A few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? (If a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with one of these, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't done that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete the assessment:

Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment. That's why I'm asking about it now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, Alex is 17. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can only continue if they:
- Stay in approved education or training, OR
- Leave education/training but register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks)

Since Alex has left school, is not in any education or training, is not working, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, the eligibility criteria are not met.

**However**, if Alex decides to:
- Return to approved education or training
- Register with a careers service or the armed services

You may become eligible at that point. If his circumstances change, you can make a claim then.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old, which is above the automatic eligibility age of 16. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can continue only if they stay in approved education or training. Alex has left school and is not in any education or training. He is not working, and has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services (which would allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education). Since none of these conditions are met, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
